thread:
maya: quick check — I built a tiny probe to reproduce duplicate side-effects when token rotates during retries. sharing logs + config here. anyone spot a flaw? :wave:

oliver: nice. does the probe toggle different jitter strategies? curious if equal-jitter vs full-jitter matters for bursts.

maya: yes, it's configurable: full, equal, and decorrelated. default run uses full-jitter in an exponential backoff.

sam: for safety, add an "auto_idempotency" toggle. if on, SDK auto-attaches Idempotency-Key for mutating endpoints. test both.

maya: done. also instrumented per-request sequence ids and server request_id echo so we can detect partial stream replays.

ci-bot: test-run: jitter-probe-2066123456 started on staging (run id: jp-2066-a). logs: /staging/jitter/jp-2066-a/logs.zip

oliver: reminder: SDKs should never overwrite an explicit Idempotency-Key header. explicit wins.

sam: agreed. policy: explicit header > auto-generated key > none. also add safe_replay_window_ms config with conservative default 500ms.

maya: initial results: auto-key + 500ms reduced duplicates on non-streamed calls by ~30%. streaming still shows rare partial-token dupes; will try stricter resume policy. uploading summary.

ci-bot: upload complete: /staging/jitter/jp-2066-a/summary.csv :white_check_mark:
thread_summary: probe to reproduce duplicates during token rotation+retries; compared jitter strategies, added auto_idempotency toggle, safe_replay_window_ms, and streaming sequence ids
